newsitem.title: UK: North Sea physical markets quiet, Brent paper ease.
newsitem.headline: North Sea physical markets quiet, Brent paper ease.

text.p: Physical discussion on North Sea crude markets was lacklustre on Monday, while Brent intermonth spreads and outright values eased lower, traders said.
Although few December North Sea cargoes remained unsold, some traders believed that most buyers had covered their requirements for this month.
"Most people have done their Christmas buying," said one trader. "(For December barrels) we'll probably won't be seeing much more buying except for optimising purposes now."
But with only a handful of end-month cargoes left, traders doubted that differentials would come under serious pressure.
Both of the Brent cargoes nominated from the paper chains on Monday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
One cargo, loading Dec 24-26, was kept early by equity holder Murphy. The other was kept by trading house J.Aron, traders said.
Jan Brent paper was trading some 65 cents down around IPE screen levels of $23.87/$23.90 a barrel at 1635 GMT.
The market retraced gains made in a rapid late rally on Friday, helped by the granting of U.N. approval for the start of Iraqi oil sales.
Intermonth Brent spreads were easier, with Jan/Feb traded at +69 cents and later talked at +66/68 cents and Feb/March traded weaker at +69 cents.
Good buying interest was already seen for first decade January barrels, after an Oseberg cargo, loading Jan 1-5, was sold by an equity holder late on Friday at a firm Dated Brent +48 cents.
The first North Sea January loading programmes are expected to be released later this week.
Three Oseberg, two or three Ekofisks, two Gullfaks and a Troll, remain unsold for December, traders said.
